title: Producer-consumer queues and backpressure

objectives.text: Trace capacity/FIFO/close-and-drain invariants without treating empty/full/rejected states as accepted data or silent eviction.
Use same-mutex wait predicates and close notifications to apply bounded backpressure while separating normal completion from cancellation/fairness/deadline guarantees.
Simulate a one-empty-slot circular FIFO with exact rejection/wraparound state, without confusing sequential behavior with concurrent SPSC correctness.

blocks.markdown: A bounded queue caps queued items, not the entire system. Our queue has positive capacity, FIFO removal and an explicit closed flag. Accepted items are appended once; a full queue must wait or reject under its declared API, never silently overwrite an older accepted event. close is idempotent, rejects all new pushes and preserves already accepted items for draining. Once closed AND empty, pop reports drained. Open-and-empty is instead temporarily empty/waiting. A queued value 0 is valid data and must not be confused with no item.

blocks.title: Track accepted, rejected and drained separately

steps.text: Capacity 2 starts open/empty. Push 0 and push 2 are accepted, giving FIFO(0,2). Push 3 when full is rejected by the nonblocking model, leaving(0,2). It was not accepted and cannot be counted as delivered.
Close leaves(0,2)queued and makes the closed flag true. Push 4 is rejected as closed. Pop returns 0, then 2; zero is a valid value, not the end marker.

The next pop reports closed-and-drained. Repeating close changes nothing. At each point accepted pushes minus popped items equals current size; rejected pushes contribute neither queued nor popped items.

blocks.caption: Expected lines: pushed None; pushed None; full None; closed None; closed None; popped 0; popped 2; drained None; ((), True). Immutable tuple state means rejected operations leave it unchanged. This is a single-thread finite nonblocking model, not a concurrent queue implementation. Capacity 1..8 and exact integer values 0..100 are own teaching bounds; None is a returned absence, not stored queue data.

blocks.markdown: The native monitor below waits for push permission with closed||count<capacity, and for pop permission with closed||count>0. The queue fields, closed flag and predicate checks use the SAME mutex. wait(unique_lock,predicate)checks before sleeping and repeats after waking; it atomically releases the mutex and blocks, then reacquires before checking. Spurious wakeups and another worker consuming the opportunity are allowed, so a notification is a hint to recheck, not an item or a stored permit. Ordinary push/pop notify the opposite class of waiter; close notifies ALL producers and consumers so each can observe closure.

blocks.caption: C++20 with -pthread, fixed ring capacity 2. Expected output: 6 15 true, then false true. One main producer sends 0..5, one consumer records FIFO items, main prints after joining. Optional<int>{0} still has a value. The close guard is declared AFTER the consumer handle, so on ordinary return/unwind it closes first, allowing drain/exit before the handle joins. No live network, allocations for ring payload, sleeps, forced cancellation or timing claim. App C++ support remains unverified.

blocks.markdown: All queue metadata and slot accesses occur under mutex_. push/pop choose their transition while holding that mutex; callbacks/processing are not run inside it. A waiting push is released by capacity becoming available or closure; after closure it returns false. pop drains remaining data, returning nullopt only after closed&&empty. Closing twice is harmless. Main closes then leaves the worker scope; the consumer finishes draining, joins, and only then are its result fields read and finally the queue/synchronization objects destroyed. If consumer construction itself fails, no worker exists to wait on the queue. The guard covers ordinary producer-scope exit assuming synchronization operations succeed; it does not recover an OS mutex failure, process crash or worker exception.

Waiting on a full bounded queue pushes pressure back to the producer; the producer must not hold an unrelated lock the consumer needs. This blocking API differs deliberately from the pure model returning full/empty. Choose waiting, explicit reject, drop-with-count, spill or upstream rate reduction from the application contract, not convenience. Dropping an uncommitted telemetry sample may be acceptable under a stated policy; dropping an accepted financial event without reconciliation is not. Queue item capacity 2 here bounds only the fixed int ring, not OS thread stacks, output storage, upstream buffers, payloads elsewhere or total process memory.

A condition-variable wait does not itself promise fairness, finite wakeup latency or an overall deadline. jthread stop requests do not automatically wake ordinary condition_variable waits; this implementation needs explicit close. A consumer that hangs outside the queue or fails before draining can stall a producer indefinitely. Production cancellation/failure propagation, timed operations using a fixed deadline, upstream admission/metrics, queue age/high-water marks and reconciliation need separate design/testing. This simple normal-path monitor is not certified for those outcomes. Tests should distinguish close-empty, close-full, waiting push/pop, draining, rejected-after-close and FIFO/exactly-once accounting, without treating repeated test success as all-schedules proof.

Independent transfer: enumerate short push/pop/close sequences at capacities1..3 and compare accepted/popped histories to a separate list reference. Include duplicate numeric values and zero; reason by acceptance history rather than deduplicating values. For a native variant, explicitly arrange a waiting consumer and close-empty, then arrange a waiting producer and close-full using test coordination, not a sleep as proof. Keep queue alive until every worker finishes and never destroy its mutex/condition variables while in use.

Sources: [condition-variable standard contract](https://eel.is/c++draft/thread.condition.condvar), [predicate wait details](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/condition_variable/wait.html), [same-mutex ordering](https://eel.is/c++draft/thread.mutex.requirements.mutex), and [jthread lifetime](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/jthread.html). BoundedRing is an authored monitor with its own close/drain policy, not a claim that the standard library supplies this queue type or that a search-result queue proposal is current standard.

An alternative capacity contract

Here c slots hold at most c-1 values because one slot is always unused. head is the NEXT READ index and tail the NEXT WRITE index,both initially 0. Empty means head==tail; full means(tail+1)%c==head. This differs from the earlier count-based monitor,which uses its full array capacity and has a close/drain policy. The Linux circular-buffer document uses the opposite head/tail naming convention,so translate by role rather than copying names.

Transitions preserve accepted FIFO order

PUSH computes next_tail before writing. If full,emit FULL and change neither slot nor index; otherwise write at tail,advance tail,and emit OK. POP on empty emits EMPTY without state changes; otherwise read at head,advance head,and print the stored integer. Zero and negative values are ordinary payloads,not empty sentinels. The code may clear a consumed slot for clarity,but occupancy is determined by indexes,not None values.

Derive size and trace wraparound

Always0<=size<=c-1,and size=(tail-head)%c under the one-empty-slot convention. At c=3:push 7, push 8 fill the usable 2 slots;push 9 rejects unchanged;pop returns 7 and head=1;push 9writes slot 2 and wraps tail=0. Stored FIFO is [8,9], size=(0-1)%3=2. Rejected operations do not consume data or advance indexes. Final output includes HEAD,TAIL,SIZE after all operations; the original starter provides push values as strings,so int(op[1]) is explicit.

Sequential simulation is not a lock-free proof

The task applies operations strictly in input order. O(c) allocated slots plus O(t) returned strings,with O(1)state work per operation and O(c+t)initialization/scan,meet c<=1000000,t<=200000. This function does not run threads and proves no atomic publication,memory-ordering,progress or race guarantees. Real SPSC needs a documented ownership/publication protocol and correct acquire/release or other synchronization on its target memory model. Arbitrary c is valid here,so modulo is required; bitmask wraparound works only for power-of-two capacity. Compare accepted/popped values and final indexes with an independent bounded list queue for exhaustive short operations and many wraps.

blocks.source:
from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math

def run_ring(capacity, ops):
    slots = [None] * capacity
    head = tail = 0
    lines = []
    for op in ops:
        if op[0] == 'PUSH':
            next_tail = (tail + 1) % capacity
            if next_tail == head:
                lines.append('FULL')
            else:
                slots[tail] = int(op[1])
                tail = next_tail
                lines.append('OK')
        elif head == tail:
            lines.append('EMPTY')
        else:
            lines.append(str(slots[head]))
            slots[head] = None
            head = (head + 1) % capacity
    return lines + [f'HEAD {head} TAIL {tail} SIZE {(tail - head) % capacity}']

print(*run_ring(3,[['PUSH','7'],['PUSH','8'],['PUSH','9'],['POP'],['PUSH','9']]), sep='\n')

summary: Capacity, FIFO and accepted-item accounting are invariants; close rejects new pushes while preserving drain. Wait on predicates under the same mutex, recheck after wake, notify all on close and join before destruction. Backpressure bounds one queue, not time, fairness, cancellation or all system memory. Practice transfer: one empty slot ring.
